subject: ACME: Third‑party IP notice protocol / litigation handover questions
messages:
From: Sara Morrow <sara.morrow@acme-corp.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question: notice protocol & evidence retention for third‑party IP claim

Ava —

We’ve received a preliminary notice from a third party alleging infringement relating to a subset of outputs generated while testing Redwood in our evaluation environment. Legal here asked me to confirm the protocol in the MSA/order form for:

- Timing and form of a notice Redwood expects us to provide (what qualifies as “notice” under the draft order form).
- Evidence preservation and what logs/outputs Redwood needs to investigate (timestamps, prompts, model + model_version, request_id).
- Whether Redwood will accept a notice routed to a single legal inbox and who the escalation contact(s) are for litigation hold coordination.

Can you point me to the right place in the contract language (draft v3) and confirm the handover steps if this escalates to a claim? We’re trying to align internal stakeholders on timeline — counsel is asking for a 48h ACK and expected turnaround for an initial assessment.

Thanks,
Sara Morrow
Senior Contracts Manager
ACME Cloud
[Attachment: ACME_MSA_notice_protocol_questions.pdf]

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Morrow <sara.morrow@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: notice protocol & evidence retention for third‑party IP claim

Sara —

Thanks for the heads up and for the PDF — I’ve shared with Legal and CS. High level answers so your team can update counsel quickly:

- ACK: we will acknowledge notice within 48 hours of receipt to the email address in the Order Form.
- Required evidence: we’ll need the request_id(s), model name + version, prompt text (if available), timestamps, and any attachments that accompanied the alleged material. We may also request samples of the third‑party’s assertion (links, screenshots).
- Routing: the simplest path is to send to legal@redwood.com; that will create a ticket and notify our on‑call contract lawyer. If you want a direct escalation contact add kimberly.park@redwood.com and she will triage.

Kimberly — can you confirm that the ACK + initial assessment SLA (48h ack, preliminary assessment within 5 business days) is acceptable given our current language? Also, I believe our Order Form has a single notice email but we should confirm the wording around "evidence" and any preservation obligations.

Ben — FYI for CS and billing implications if this becomes a formal claim.

—Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Account Manager, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, sara.morrow@acme-corp.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: notice protocol & evidence retention for third‑party IP claim

Sara / Ava —

Thanks — I reviewed the current MSA (draft v3 attached) and have a short set of legal clarifications and recommended language. Key points:

1) Notice definition & delivery
- Current: notice must be "in writing to the address specified in the Order Form." Recommend: explicitly allow email to legal@redwood.com to satisfy "in writing" to avoid routing delays.

2) Evidence & logs
- We should be explicit that Customer is required to provide the sample outputs and the corresponding request_id(s) and timestamps. For Redwood’s investigative purposes we will request model name and model_version; however, we cannot disclose third‑party confidential materials.

3) Preservation period
- Recommend adding a 90‑day preservation obligation for the customer to retain relevant logs/samples while investigation is active. This is a limited, reasonable ask and helps triage.

4) Defense vs. Reimbursement split
- The current MSA leans toward Redwood defending at our option for software/process issues, but there’s ambiguity on AI‑output claims. I propose adding a defend/reimburse matrix for:
  • Model defects (Redwood to defend)
  • Customer prompt/content misuse (Customer to defend)
  • Unsupported training data claims (mutual allocation or insurance carve‑out)

5) Escalation & litigation handover
- Suggested process: ACK within 48h; initial technical assessment within 5 business days; if claim plausibly implicates model behavior we will:
  a) engage Redwood Legal (copy kimberly.park@redwood.com),
  b) request formal claim materials and a signed declaration from Customer to permit log access,
  c) if litigation starts, Redwood will coordinate evidence export through a secure portal (DocuSign + SFTP per the Order Form addendum).

I’ve attached a short matrix (Redwood_defend_vs_reimburse_matrix.xlsx) and a proposed redline for the notice / preservation language. If ACME can accept email notice and a 90‑day preservation window, that should close the bulk of counsel's asks.

[Attachment: Redwood_defend_vs_reimburse_matrix.xlsx]

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Morrow <sara.morrow@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: notice protocol & evidence retention for third‑party IP claim

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear matrix and the preservation suggestion. Two follow ups from ACME Legal:

1) Email notice: they are OK with legal@redwood.com as long as the Order Form explicitly lists that address (they want no ambiguity about what satisfies notice).
2) 90 days: they will accept the 90‑day preservation but want language that allows shorter notice if Redwood requires faster access for remediation; e.g., "Customer shall preserve for at least 90 days unless Redwood reasonably requests expedited access."

Finally, procurement asked whether insurance offsets are in scope — if Redwood expects defense for model defects, do you expect ACME’s insurance to be primary in any allocation or should this be addressed as an offset only after indemnity is resolved? Counsel suggested a short call.

If we can close the Order Form language today, we can route to procurement for signature (ACME prefers to push final executed order forms this week).

Sara

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: sara.morrow@acme-corp.com
Cc: ava.chen@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: notice protocol & evidence retention for third‑party IP claim

Sara —

Quick reply on the insurance/offset question: Redwood’s baseline position is that indemnity triggers do not change insurance primacy — the party responsible under the defend/reimburse matrix should seek recovery from its insurer first, and we allow offsets only after indemnity obligations are allocated. Practically:

- If Redwood defends because of a model defect, we will manage the defense. If a covered payment is ultimately awarded to Customer, we’ll discuss coordination with insurers as part of settlement — but indemnity obligations remain the guiding contractual allocation.

Kimberly is available for a 30m call if ACME counsel wants to walk through the proposed redline and carve‑outs. Ava — can you coordinate a window today or tomorrow? If ACME is ready to accept the email address in the Order Form and the 90‑day + expedited access carve, we’ll push the redline to procurement for signature.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
